text: CPR (BeenyHail/CPR at commit 9ecd685) is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial). It may be run as a comparison baseline, but its code must not be copied into PDFPundit (clean-room rule); any commercial use of PDFPundit rules out shipping it.

CPR's Step 2 LLM call posts only model, prompt and stream to a local Ollama server (llama3.1:8b, localhost:11434); it sets no temperature, seed or other sampling options, so a CPR run has no deterministic mode as published. Reproducible CPR baselines would need a local patch adding options (temperature 0, fixed seed), which must be reported as a deviation.

qpdf reconstructs a damaged cross-reference table by default; --suppress-recovery turns this heuristic recovery off. A qpdf repair baseline therefore runs with defaults (recovery on), and the --suppress-recovery run is a strict-parse control, not a repair setting.
quote: Prevents qpdf from attempting to reconstruct a file's cross reference table when there are errors reading objects from the file.

text: qpdf --check is a syntactic check only: by its own manual it does not validate page content or semantic correctness. As a conformance oracle it must be paired with a model-based checker (Arlington) and a second validator (pdfcpu strict); exit 0 does not mean the repair is correct.
quote: Note that qpdf does not perform any validation of the actual PDF page content or semantic correctness of the PDF file. It merely checks that the PDF file is syntactically valid.

text: mutool clean exposes four cumulative garbage-collection levels (-g unused objects, -gg plus xref compaction, -ggg plus duplicate-object merge, -gggg plus duplicate-stream check); these, with -s (sanitize content streams), define the MuPDF best-of option set for repair baselines.
quote: "\t-gggg\tin addition to -ggg check streams for duplication\n"

text: Ghostscript's PDF interpreter repairs or ignores problems by default; -dPDFSTOPONERROR makes it stop instead. A Ghostscript repair baseline (pdfwrite re-distill) therefore runs with defaults, and -dPDFSTOPONERROR is a strict control.
quote: The PDF interpreter normally tries to repair, or ignore, all problems encountered in PDF files.

text: pdf.js recovers by default: its getDocument option stopAtErrors defaults to false, and only when set true does it reject getOperatorList, getTextContent and rendering on unparseable data. The pdf.js baseline therefore runs with defaults, and stopAtErrors: true is the strict control.
quote: instead of attempting to recover whatever possible of the data. The default value is `false`.
